title: Research better document parsing than PDF.js (Docling, marker, unstructured, local OCR)
description: Why: LibreChat's built-in document_parser (packages/api/src/files/documents/crud.ts, pdfToText) uses pdfjs-dist getTextContent and joins items with spaces per page. It loses layout, tables, headings and reading order in multi-column PDFs, and returns nothing for scanned pages (OCR needed). What: evaluate Docling (IBM, Python, layout+table aware, exposes a CLI/server), marker, unstructured and a local OCR option (tesseract/paddle) for quality vs cost on this machine (RTX 3060 12 GB shared with llama-server). Decide the integration seam: LibreChat already has pluggable extraction via fileConfig.ocr (strategy + supportedMimeTypes, see getUploadExtractedTextPlan in packages/api/src/protection/files.ts) and RAG_API_URL; a local HTTP service exposing an OCR-compatible or RAG-compatible interface would plug in without forking parser code. Output: a short spec under docs/superpowers/specs/ with the chosen tool, resource footprint, and the config to wire it. Depends on the PDF-to-text routing change (fileConfig override in librechat.yaml) being verified first.
